Hi everyone, is there anything in Mathlib for the Fubini-Study metric on ℂℙ^(n-1), or for Kähler manifolds?

What I've found so far: docs#Projectivization looks purely algebraic, with no topology, measure or metric on it. Searching for Kähler turns up docs#KaehlerDifferential, which is unrelated, and docs#Orientation.kahler, which is a complex-valued bilinear map on a two-dimensional real inner product space rather than manifold theory. Nothing for Fubini-Study that I can see.

Am I missing something under a different name? I've got a fair bit of this staged in my own repo and would rather build on Mathlib than duplicate it as I want to be more aligned to Mathlib going forward.

We do not have the Fubini-Study metric.

For various reasons, differential geometry has developed much more slowly than other fields in Mathlib. In particular we still lack the definitions of symplectic manifolds and Kähler manifolds.

The good news is that we do have a definition for Riemannian manifolds docs#IsRiemannianManifold but the theory is still relatively recent and I think we may not even have any concrete instances of it within Mathlib.

So you could define the Fubini-Study as a Riemannian metric but you wouldn't be able to state that it is Kähler or even to do much with it in the near term.

Thanks, that's really useful.

It's actually the Fubini-Study measure I need rather than the metric and that seems to sidestep this problem entirely.

I'm working out what upstreaming it would involve since a few things underneath it don't look like they're in Mathlib either. Good to know that the Metric route is closed for now before I spent time on it.

If you just want the measure then you just need the metric in the sense of docs#MetricSpace since then the measure (up to scale) is the Hausdorff measure docs#MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure And the metric has the tidy formula d([v],[w])=arccos⁡∣⟨v,w⟩∣∥v∥∥w∥d([v], [w]) = \arccos\frac{|\langle v, w\rangle|}{\|v\|\|w\|}d([v],[w])=arccos∥v∥∥w∥∣⟨v,w⟩∣​.

Mind you, it might not be so easy to prove things using this construction, depending on what your goals are.

THanks, That's a useful pointer I hadn't thought about coming at it through Hausdorff measure.

Can I check something more basic though, what I've built is the pushforward of normalised Haar on Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin N) ℂ through the orbit map and I've proved it's the unique U(N)-invariant Borel probability measure, in the sense that any invariant probability measure equals it. Is that right?

Is that characterisation on its own enough to call it the Fubini-Study measure or would the metric construction pin down something that the uniqueness argument doesn't?
